Summary: The command: Burn sacrifices that became impure (Leviticus 7:19). Flesh that touched any unclean thing was burned with fire, not eaten.
Commandment: Burn sacrifices that became impure, as prescribed in Leviticus 7:19.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: Flesh that touched any unclean thing was burned with fire, not eaten — a ceremonial law of the spoiled sacrifice. Its goal was to keep impurity from spreading through holy food, the touched flesh destroyed rather than eaten. The evil was the unclean sacrifice kept and eaten as if the touch did not matter. It restrained that by the fire: the flesh was burned, and the impurity died with it instead of passing into the eater.
